newsitem.title: UK: Guardian profits fall but dividend raised.
newsitem.headline: Guardian profits fall but dividend raised.

text.p: Insurance group Guardian Royal Exchange Plc reported a fall in trading profits on Tuesday but said it was raising the dividend payout for the year by 11.1 percent to 10.0 pence per share.

Trading profits for the year of 281 million pounds ($458.4 million) compared with profits of 340 million pounds for 1995 and included 39 million pounds in restructuring costs. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)

Guardian chief executive John Robins said the results were achieved in the face of continuing competitive pressure. He also blamed abnormally severe weather conditions in North America and adverse weather and continuing subsidence costs in the UK.

He said the group continued to withdraw from non-core, non-performing markets and had three objectives: greater attention to customer needs, greater focus on the cost base and increasing return on shareholders funds.
While there was still pressures on margins Robins said there were bright spots.

"We have seen some hardening of premiums in selected sectors and regions, such as UK motor insurance, and the difficult conditions in the German market have not been as severe as had been forecast by some commentators," he said.
The results included provisions for the integration of the Legal & General business and fundamental restructuring of the UK insurance business.
